title: Scheduled Model Upgrade: Tenant Notification, Canary Rollout, and Rollback Playbook
author: Ravi Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the cross-functional process for scheduled model upgrades that affect enterprise tenants (hosted, dedicated, and private). It covers pre-upgrade validation, tenant communications, canary rollout strategy, automated and manual rollback criteria, post-upgrade verification, and escalation paths. The goal is to ensure predictable, low-risk upgrades with clear customer-facing communication and rapid mitigation if quality or reliability regressions are detected.

Scope:
- Applies to any non-trivial model version change (weights or tokenizer changes, quantization/format changes, runtime ABI changes) scheduled during standard maintenance windows.
- Includes Hosted API customers, Redwood Dedicated tenants, and Private deployments where Redwood coordinates or provides upgrade artifacts.
- Excludes entirely internal-only test model swaps performed in isolated staging environments.

Owners & Roles:
- Product Release Lead: triage owner for upgrade schedule and customer notices. (Owner: Product Release Manager)
- Customer Success Lead: primary point of contact for affected enterprise customers and for communicating impacts. (Owner: Customer Success Manager)
- Runtime/Serving Owner: executes canary rollout and rollback, validates metrics, and performs emergency rollback when required. (Owner: Serving Runtime SRE)
- Observability Owner: ensures dashboards, alerts, and synthetic tests are active and tuned for the upgrade. (Owner: Observability Engineer)
- Security/Compliance Owner: confirms approval for upgrades that touch sensitive data or private tenants. (Owner: Security PM)

Pre-Upgrade Checklist (minimum gating criteria):
1) Release artifacts prepared and smoke-tested in staging: model binaries, container images, migration scripts.
2) Canary config baked: percentage targets, tenant selectors, fallback model mapping, and time-limited canary windows.
3) Automated sanity suite green on staging: tokenization, generation smoke prompts, and embedding regression checks.
4) SLO baseline capture: last 14 days of latency (p50/p95), error rate, token cost per request, and model quality evals on canonical prompt set.
5) Observability readiness: dashboards, anomaly detectors, and SLO alert thresholds verified.
6) Communication artifacts ready: customer email template, incident-communication template, and support-runbook snippets.
7) Rollback playbooks validated in a dry-run: scripted rollback and clear state reconciliation steps.
8) Approval gate signoffs: Product, CS, Serving Runtime, and Security as required.

Scheduling & Tenant Notification:
- Maintenance window: prefer low-traffic windows in tenant region (e.g., 0100–0400 local). For multi-region tenants, coordinate a single targeted rollout with time-zone-aware notices.
- Notification cadence (enterprise tenants):
  * 14 days before: high-level notice with expected impact, upgrade window, and opt-out instructions (if available).
  * 3 days before: detailed technical notice including canary percentage, API version pin instructions, and rollback SLAs.
  * 24 hours before: reminder and pre-upgrade checklist for tenant (recommended testing plan).
  * 1 hour before: imminent reminder via Slack/email to named contacts.
- Communication templates: include standard subject lines, summary sections, and a clear “what to do if you see issues” section. See template snippets below.

Canary Rollout Strategy (recommended default):
1) Stage 0 — Internal smoke (0% tenant traffic): run all internal synthetic scenarios and trace logs for 60–120 minutes.
2) Stage 1 — Very small external canary (1–2% of traffic or single volunteer tenant): monitor for 30–60 minutes.
3) Stage 2 — Expanded canary (5–10% of traffic or a small cohort of non-critical tenants): monitor for 60–120 minutes.
4) Stage 3 — Progressive ramp (25% then 50%): if metrics stable, increase to these bands with 2× monitoring intervals.
5) Stage 4 — Full rollout (100%): gated final decision after passing Stage 3 checks.

For Dedicated/Private customers where per-tenant pinning is supported: use tenant selector labels to apply the model only to specified tenants; prefer volunteer tenants for initial stages. If tenant declines participation, do not include them in the canary.

Automated Metrics & Acceptance Criteria (must be continuously evaluated during canary):
- Latency: p50 and p95 should not regress by more than +20% (absolute threshold: p95 <= 800ms for text-generation default profile).
- Error rate: total 5xx and request-failures must remain <= existing baseline + 0.1 percentage points and absolute <= 0.5%.
- Token cost: average tokens-per-request should not increase more than +10% without documented cause.
- Quality regression: automated eval on canonical prompt set must show no >3% drop in primary metric (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity or custom eval).
- Fuzzy anomaly detection: anomaly score on model outputs (semantic drift detector) must remain below configured threshold for the canary cohort.

If any single critical threshold is violated, the system will:
- Immediately pause canary ramping.
- Notify the on-call Serving Runtime engineer and Customer Success Lead.
- Trigger a fast rollback if the issue materially impacts customer SLAs (see Rollback Criteria).

Rollback Criteria & Procedure:
Decision matrix (examples):
- Severity 1 (service-impacting, persistent): automatic rollback within 15 minutes. Examples: sustained p95 > 1200ms, error rate > 1.5% sustained over 5 minutes, or loss of model responses for a tenant.
- Severity 2 (quality-impacting but non-blocking): pause and evaluate; manual rollback within 60 minutes if no mitigation. Examples: quality metric drop > 6% on canonical eval or customer-reported misbehavior on production prompts.
- Severity 3 (transient anomalies): continue monitoring; remediation via config patch or retry logic. Examples: short-lived spike in latencies or intermittent downstream infra error.

Rollback steps (serving runtime owner executes):
1) Re-route affected traffic back to prior pinned model version using the canary control plane API. Example CLI: redwoodctl rollout --tenant <tenant-id> --from-version <new> --to-version <previous> --reason "automatic-rollback: latency regressed"
2) Validate traffic routing and confirm that pre-upgrade model is serving for the affected tenant(s).
3) Re-run smoke generation tests against the restored model and confirm baseline metrics.
4) Notify Customer Success and the customer POC immediately with the rollback summary and next steps.
5) Open a post-incident triage ticket and schedule a cross-team RCA within 72 hours.

Post-Upgrade Verification (after full rollout):
- 24-hour and 7-day checks: confirm sustained SLO adherence and no regression in quality metrics.
- Customer validation: deliver a short validation checklist to the customer POC to confirm expected behavior.
- Billing/Cost reconciliation: capture token-cost delta and alert finance if variance > 8% month-to-date.

Observability Playbook (quick commands and dashboards):
- Dashboards to monitor: Model Serving Overview, Canary Cohort Health, Latency Heatmap (by tenant), Error Distribution, Model Quality Snapshot.
- Quick checks (CLI / API):
  * Get canary assignment: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/<tenant-id>/model-assignment
  * Fetch model metrics: redwood-metrics query "model.latency.p95{model=\"<model-name>\"}" --last 15m
  * Trigger synthetic test: curl -X POST https://ops.redwood.ai/synthetics/run -d '{"test_suite":"upgrade-smoke","model":"<model-name>"}'

Customer-Facing Messaging (templates):
- Subject: "Planned model upgrade for <Tenant Name> — maintenance window <date/time>"
- Body: include short summary, expected impact (likely none), canary approach, opt-out link (if applicable), contact info, and guidance for quick verification.
- Incident messaging (if rollback occurs): short description of customer exposure, actions taken (rollback executed), expected follow-up timeline, and link to RCA.

Support Triage Flow (if customers report issues during or after upgrade):
1) First-line support: run the tenant validation checklist and capture examples (request_id, timestamps, prompt text, returned output).
2) If reproducible, escalate to Serving Runtime on-call with logs, metrics, and customer-observed sample.
3) If issue is quality-related, hand off to Applied ML & Evals team for evaluation against canonical prompt sets.
4) Engage Product & CS to determine whether to pause rollout for additional testing or to rollback.

Runbook Attachments (snippets):
- Example canary API payload: {\"canary_percent\":5,\"cohort_selector\":\"label:volunteer\",\"max_duration_min\":120}
- Example rollback CLI snippet: redwoodctl rollback --scope tenant --id <tenant-id> --target-version <sha-or-tag> --reason "fast-rollback: automatic-threshold"

Postmortem & RCA expectations:
- For any automatic rollback or Severity 1 outage: publish a written RCA within 72 hours, with timeline, root cause, corrective actions, and responsible owners for fixes.
- For Severity 2 escalations: summary RCA within 7 days and a follow-up plan for model tuning or augmenting synthetic tests.

Customer Success Playbook Actions (for CSMs):
- Pre-upgrade: confirm POC has a test plan and knows how to pin model versions if they want a freeze.
- During canary: maintain an open channel with the customer POC and provide live updates at milestone gates.
- After rollback: coordinate follow-up postmortem call and share remediation timelines.

Appendix: Example Email Template (short)
Subject: Planned model upgrade for <TenantName> — <Date/Window>
Hi <POC>,
We will be performing a scheduled model upgrade that may affect inference quality for a small subset of requests. We are using a conservative canary rollout and expect no disruption for most customers. If you prefer to be excluded from the canary, reply to this message before <X>.
Planned window: <Date/Time>
What we will do: staged canary, monitoring, and rapid rollback if thresholds are violated.
How you can test: run the quick verification checklist attached.
Who to contact: <CS POC contact> (phone/slack)
Thanks,
Customer Success (Redwood)

Appendix: Quick Verification Checklist for Tenants
- Run 5 representative prompts and compare responses to baseline.
- Verify latency for 10 requests does not exceed usual p95 by >40%.
- Report any unexpected formatting, hallucination, or API errors with timestamps and request IDs.
